learn.title: Making a choice
learn.body: A program can choose what to do. `if` runs a block only when its condition is true. `else` runs when it is not. The indented lines belong to the `if` or `else` above them.

learn.title: if and else
learn.body: Here `temp > 25` is true, so it prints hot. The `else` block is skipped.

learn.title: Colons and indents
learn.body: Each `if` and `else` line ends with a colon. The lines under it are indented by four spaces. The indent is how Python knows which lines belong together. A missing colon or indent is an error.

learn.title: More than two paths
learn.body: Python checks from the top and stops at the first true condition. 75 is not at least 90 but is at least 70, so it prints B.

learn.title: Even or odd?
learn.body: Code: `n = 4`, then `if n % 2 == 0:` prints even, `else:` prints odd.
steps: `n % 2` is 0, because 4 divides by 2 with no remainder
`0 == 0` is true, so the `if` block runs
It prints even, and the `else` block is skipped

learn.body: In an if, elif, else chain only one block ever runs.

questions.prompt: `x = 3`. `if x > 5:` prints big, `else:` prints small. What prints?
questions.explanation: 3 is not greater than 5, so the `else` block runs.

questions.prompt: What must an `if` line end with?
questions.explanation: Python needs a colon at the end of `if`, `elif` and `else` lines.

questions.prompt: `score = 75`. `if score >= 90` prints A, `elif score >= 70` prints B, `else` prints C. What prints?
questions.explanation: The first test fails, the second passes, so it prints B and stops.

questions.prompt: Use \_\_ to run code when the `if` condition is false.
questions.explanation: `else` has no condition. It catches everything the `if` did not.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of an if and else in order.
steps: Write `if` and a condition, ending in a colon
Indent the lines to run when true
Indent the lines to run when false
questions.explanation: The `if` part comes first with its own indented lines, then the `else` part.

questions.prompt: `n = 7`. `if n % 2 == 0:` prints even, `else:` prints odd. What prints?
questions.explanation: 7 % 2 is 1, not 0, so the condition is false and it prints odd.
